objectives: This class will cover some special topics in the field of signal integrity (SI), power integrity (PI), and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) as detailed in the course content below. The theories of these topics will be introduced in class, and students are required to complete several homework. For PI topics, the homework will be based on LTspice, while for other topics the homework is mostly Python-coding problems. This course is not a sequel of the course Signal Integrity and Electromagnetic Compatibility of the spring semester, so students are welcome to take this course even if you have not taken the spring-semester one. Undergraduates are also welcome to take this course as long as you have studied Electromagnetic, Complex Analysis, and Signals and Systems.
content:
1. Transmission line theory
* TEM mode
* Dielectric models
* Quasi-TEM mode
* Conductor models
* Time-domain reflectometry
* Surface roughness
2. Causality
* Causality theorems
* Causality assessment
3. Power integrity
* Power delivery framework
* Buck converter analysis and design
* Voltage mode control
* Current mode control
* PDN analysis and design
4. Selected EMC topics
books:
1. Stephen Hall and Howard Heck, Advanced Signal Integrity for High Speed Digital Designs, Wiley-IEEE Press, 2009. ( https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/book/5361024 )
2. Clayton Paul, Introduction to Electromagnetic Compatibility, Wiley, 2005. ( https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/0471758159 ) Both books can be downloaded if you are within NCU‘s ip.
3. M. Swaminathan and A. Engin, Power Integrity Modeling and Design for Semiconductors and Systems, Prentice Hall, 2008. (Available at library)
4. Eric Bogatin, Signal and Power Integrity – Simplified, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 2010, Ch 13. (Available at library)
5. S. Grivet-Talocia and B. Gustavsen, Passive macromodeling: Theory and applications, John Wiley ＆ Sons, 2016. (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781119140931)
grading_policy: Homework 100％, including about 12 homework each account for 8~10% depending on the complexity.
